liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Jazzy groove with stupendous Jerry lead; subdued Pig rap melds perfectly [5]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Identified as far and away the best performance of this tune [10]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Superb 26-minute performance, first time combined with Morning Dew [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.smith.94581.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 195 min [1]
- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.miller.79057.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 182 min; rated 4.91/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Described as jinglin' janglin' with pure, great sound quality and quantity; Band reaches happy medium between spaced-out jazz and Pig's rap; Charlie Miller recording features stunning sound quality [6][9][12][15]
- **gd1972-05-18.sdb.lai.146.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 25 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Few bars of White Rabbit played after Chinatown Shuffle [11]
- Venue was half-empty, a small lecture hall within the museum [13]
- Less spectacular than others, but consistently well played with strong upgrades [8]
- Looser and trippier than earlier Wembley and Newcastle shows [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.smith.94581.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rex Jackson; transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: Soundboard > Master Reel (Rex Jackson) [1]. Also: Matt Smith supplied original discs; noise from reel generation attenuated [1]
- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.miller.79057.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D [2]
- **gd1972-05-18.sdb.lai.146.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: master reel>>sdb>>?>>dat>>cdr [3]
